title: Personal Hygiene & Self-Care
subtitle: Not why you wash. How you run it yourself without being reminded.
objectives: Build a morning and evening routine in a fixed order
List what a personal care kit contains
Know when each supply needs restocking
Explain why a routine beats a reminder
Take over the job of asking for what you need

cards.title: You already know what to do. This is about who runs it.
cards.text: Health class covers why. This is the part where the job moves from your parents to you.

cards.title: A routine is a fixed order, not a list
cards.text: A list needs a decision at every line. An order runs itself, because each step tells you the next one.
points: **The last step is the cue** for the next.

cards.title: Six things, and when each runs out
cards.text: Tap through. The second line is the signal to say something before it is empty.

question.text: Why does a fixed order work better than a checklist?
options: Each step cues the next, so you stop deciding
It takes less time in total
question.explain: Removing the decision is the whole mechanism. That is why the order has to stay the same.

cards.title: Your loadout is checked before the match, not during
cards.text: Nobody sorts their gear mid-fight. Everything is prepared while there is time, so the run needs no decisions.
points: **A morning is the expensive part of the day.**
**So the preparing happens the night before.**

cards.title: A morning order that fits in ten minutes
cards.text: Write yours once, in the order you actually do it. Then stop rewriting it.

question.text: Deodorant works best applied to skin that is still damp.
question.explain: Clean and dry. On damp skin it slides off and does far less.

cards.title: Halfway
cards.text: Part 2 is restocking and taking the job over. Stretch first.

cards.title: The skill is noticing before it is empty
cards.text: Anyone can notice an empty tube. The useful skill is saying something while there is still a week left.

cards.title: Open the spare, then say so
cards.text: The moment you start the last one is the moment to tell someone. Not the moment it runs out.
points: **Check the whole kit** on the same day each month.
**One message is enough.** You have done your part.

cards.title: The fuel light is not the plan
cards.text: A warning light means you have already left it late. Drivers who never run dry are watching the gauge, not the light.
points: **Not when something starts making a noise.**

cards.title: The evening order does tomorrow's work
cards.text: Everything you do at night is a decision your morning self does not have to make.
points: **Towel hung spread out**, so it dries.

question.text: When should you tell someone a supply is running low?
options: When you open the last one
At the end of the month
question.explain: Starting the last one is the signal. Empty means somebody has to fix it today.

cards.title: This is the year the routine has to change
cards.text: Your body started making demands it did not make two years ago. The routine has to grow with it.
points: **Clothes change daily**, not when they look dirty.
**Changing the routine is not a failure.**

terms.def: A fixed order of steps where each one cues the next.
The supplies and tools you need to run your own routine.
Replacing a supply before it runs out, not after.
Doing a small job on a schedule so a big one never arrives.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **Open the last one, then say so.**

options: A fixed order where each step cues the next
Doing it at a different time each day
quiz.explain: It removes the decision. That is why the order must not change.
quiz.objective: Build a morning and evening routine in a fixed order

quiz.text: Why is the evening the right time to pack a bag?
options: It removes a decision from the busiest part of the day
quiz.explain: Prepare when it is cheap; execute when it is expensive. Mornings are expensive.
quiz.objective: Build a morning and evening routine in a fixed order

quiz.text: Which belongs in a personal care kit?
quiz.explain: Supplies that run out, plus tools like nail clippers and a comb that do not.
quiz.objective: List what a personal care kit contains

quiz.text: Which of these is a tool rather than a supply?
quiz.explain: Tools do not run out. They only get lost, which is why they need one home.
quiz.objective: List what a personal care kit contains

quiz.text: How often should a toothbrush be replaced?
options: About every three months, or when the bristles splay
quiz.explain: Splayed bristles stop reaching the gum line, which is where plaque builds.
quiz.objective: Know when each supply needs restocking

quiz.text: When is the right moment to say a supply is running low?
options: When you open the last one
Two weeks after it runs out
quiz.explain: Opening the last one leaves time. Empty means someone has to solve it today.
quiz.objective: Know when each supply needs restocking

quiz.text: Checking your whole kit on the same day each month is a useful habit.
quiz.explain: True. A fixed check date means nothing depends on you happening to notice.
quiz.objective: Know when each supply needs restocking

quiz.text: Deodorant should be applied to skin that is:
quiz.explain: On damp skin it slides off and does much less than it should.
quiz.objective: Build a morning and evening routine in a fixed order

quiz.text: How should a towel be hung after use?
options: Folded in half on a hook
quiz.explain: A damp bunched towel grows bacteria quickly. Spread out, and changed weekly.
quiz.objective: List what a personal care kit contains

options: Small jobs on a schedule so a big one never arrives
quiz.explain: It is the same idea as servicing a car rather than waiting for a noise.
quiz.objective: Explain why a routine beats a reminder

quiz.text: Needing to change your routine as you grow means the old one failed.
quiz.explain: False. Your body's demands changed, so the routine changes with it.
quiz.objective: Take over the job of asking for what you need

quiz.text: What is the point of taking over your own care routine?
options: It stops depending on someone else remembering for you
quiz.explain: The job moves from being managed to being yours. That is the skill this week teaches.
quiz.objective: Take over the job of asking for what you need

teacher.summary: The TLE strand handles the same topic as MAPEH Health week 10 from a completely different angle, and the two are written not to overlap. Health explains why the body changed; this one is about ownership: a fixed routine order, a kit he is responsible for, and the specific skill of flagging a supply while there is still a week of it left. The restocking rule — say something when you open the last one — is the concrete thing to hold him to, because it converts a vague expectation into a checkable action.
discussion: Ask him to say his morning routine in order, out loud, and see whether it is actually fixed.
Ask what happens to a morning when one item cannot be found.
Ask him which supply in his kit is closest to running out right now.
Ask what he would put in an evening routine to make a school morning easier.
teacher.extension: Have him write his morning and evening routines on one card each and put them where he can see them. Then let him run both for a week and change one thing.
misconceptions: 'A routine is just a list.' A list needs a decision at every line; a routine is an order that cues itself.
'You restock when something runs out.' Opening the last one is the signal, not the empty container.
'Deodorant works better on damp skin.' Clean and dry, or most of it slides off.
'Changing your routine means the old one was wrong.' Your body changed, so the routine has to.
